risks.note: Listed first among the MD&A's Threats: 'Unpredictable costs for base substrates severely threaten profit margins.' With a net profit margin of 2.58% and an operating profit margin of 3.84% in FY26, a small move in substrate cost is enough to erase profitability.
risks.risk: Input cost volatility in base substrates

risks.note: The MD&A states that the 'Inflow of cheap Chinese imports continues to erode margins and disrupt quality perception in the market' - a structural pricing ceiling on a domestically produced, undifferentiated decorative print product.
risks.risk: Cheap Chinese imports eroding price and quality perception

risks.note: 'Currency volatility has escalated import costs, requiring proactive procurement and pricing strategies.' The Company reports NIL export earnings and NIL formal imports on CIF basis, so it carries FX cost exposure through domestic pricing of imported inputs without any natural export hedge.

The credit-risk note in the financial-statements section (carried in the sibling profile bundle, not in this one) records that 'The company has very high concentration of credit risk to a single customer which is a related party' and the geographic-information note shows total revenue from customers is essentially all revenue generated from related parties, namely Marshalls Enterprises India Pvt. Ltd. - an enterprise over which KMP exercise significant influence. Loss or repricing of this single counterparty would remove nearly the whole revenue base, and receivables from it ballooned during FY26 (current ratio fell from 7.36 to 4.23).
risks.risk: Extreme single-customer and related-party revenue concentration

risks.note: Management itself flags this: 'The Company being a small-cap company and the conservative market in which it operates is a cause of concern from the point of view of operating profits to the Company.' Total FY26 sales were Rs. 4.27 crores - a scale at which fixed costs and a single machine outage are material.
risks.risk: Sub-scale operations in a conservative market

risks.note: The MFP (Modular Furniture & Profile) line recorded NIL sales in FY26 against Rs. 47.29 Lakhs a year earlier, and the ratio note attributes the variance to 'The company has discontinued its one of the segment of the business of furniture which affected overall efficiency of business'. All operational focus now consolidates into Digital Wallpaper and Catalogue manufacturing, while warehousing income fell 10% and franchisee commission income also declined - so growth rests on one product line.
risks.risk: Narrowed revenue base after exiting modular furniture, with two declining service lines

risks.note: The FY27 turnover target of 25% leans on an export push that so far consists of leads from a single first-time exhibition at Frankfurt in January 2026; management is only 'hopeful that once the current global turmoil settles, we will be able to derive good orders from the world market'. The Company recorded NIL FOB value of exports in both FY26 and FY25.
risks.risk: Export ambition is unproven and conditional on global conditions

risks.note: The Directors' Report states that a Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27 of SEBI LODR 'is not applicable to the Company as it does not fall under the criteria of Paid up Share Capital of Rs. 10 Crore and Turnover of Rs. 25 Crores', and the Company is not required to submit an Annual Secretarial Compliance Report to the stock exchange. Combined with the related-party-dominated revenue model, this leaves fewer external checks on the arm's-length assertion.
risks.risk: Reduced external governance oversight given size thresholds
